Home / Services / Fuel system and ethanol problems

Boat fuel system repair: water in fuel, ethanol damage, pumps, injectors, carburetors

Florida's ethanol gasoline absorbs water from humid air and separates in the tank. The result is surging, stalling, varnished injectors, and rotted lines. Mechanics fix the system and set you up to prevent it.

When
Surging at mid-range, stalling, fuel smell, water in the separator bowl, a boat that sat for months.
Time on site
1 to 4 hours
What it usually costs here
$200 to $600 for lines, filters, and bulbs; pumps $400 to $900; injector sets and carburetor rebuilds $500 to $1,200.

What's included

  • Fuel quality test for water and phase separation
  • Fuel-water separator and primer bulb replacement
  • Fuel line and anti-siphon valve replacement with ethanol-rated line
  • Low- and high-pressure fuel pump replacement
  • Injector cleaning or replacement; carburetor rebuilds on older engines
  • Tank inspection, pickup and sender check
  • Stabilizer and storage advice

In Tampa Bay specifically

Humidity in the Tampa Bay summer is the enemy. Boats that sit from June to October without stabilizer are the fall no-start calls.

Engines

  • Yamaha
  • Mercury
  • Suzuki
  • Honda Marine
  • Evinrude and Johnson

Questions we get

Should I use ethanol-free gas?

If you can get it, yes. Several marinas on the bay sell it. If not, stabilize every fill and keep the tank full in storage.

My primer bulb never gets hard.

Air leak or a bad bulb, check valve, or pickup. It is one of the quickest fixes on the list and one of the most common causes of a no-start.
